tagline: Up the Skagit and over Washington Pass at 5,477 feet.
intro: SR 20 leaves Sedro-Woolley up the Skagit River, through Concrete and Rockport and Marblemount and into the national park, then through Newhalem and the narrow Diablo Canyon to Diablo Lake. It hairpins around the lake's southern arm, goes on to Ross Lake, follows Ruby and Canyon creeks up over Rainy Pass and then Washington Pass at 5,477 feet, and swings through one more hairpin on the way down into the Methow Valley and Winthrop.

The state tried a wagon road over Cascade Pass in the 1890s, and floods took most of it. This route opened on September 2, 1972, and Winthrop dressed itself up as an Old West town to meet the traffic.

moments.title: Concrete
moments.text: Baker and Cement City, each with a cement plant, merged in 1909 and settled on the name Concrete, and the town's tall silos turn up in the film This Boy's Life.

moments.title: Diablo Lake
moments.text: Rock ground to flour by the glaciers hangs in the water and turns the reservoir turquoise, and the road wraps around its southern arm in a long hairpin past a viewpoint.

moments.title: Washington Pass
moments.text: On the highway's first weekend some 8,000 people came up to this overlook, where a short trail faces Liberty Bell Mountain and the road lies 700 feet below.

practical: WSDOT closes the highway between mileposts 134 and 171 each winter, typically from late November until late April or early May, for snowfall and avalanche risk.
